This ensures that risks are identified and appropriately managed, and that security requirements are properly defined.

An inventory of organisational assets relevant to information processing, including OT, shall be in place. The inventory shall include all attributes necessary for management and maintenance. It shall also cover remote assets, cloud environments and assets that are regularly connected to the network infrastructure but are not under the organisation’s control. The completeness and accuracy of the inventory shall be periodically verified at intervals commensurate with the frequency of changes.

The information within all information systems shall be classified on the basis of an explicit risk assessment. A defined impact classification methodology, which forms part of the established risk management methodology, shall be applied for this purpose.

Internet-facing information systems and email communications shall be compliant at all times with the mandatory standards as published on the website of the Netherlands Standardisation Forum. Compliance shall be monitored using the measurements provided by internet.nl. All components shall be configured to ensure optimal security without compromising the functionality of the service provided.

For public web traffic involving sensitive data, at least publicly trusted Organisation Validated (OV) certificates shall be used. For internal web traffic involving sensitive data, at least publicly trusted Organisation OV certificates or private PKIo certificates shall be used. More stringent certificate requirements may arise from a risk assessment, connection conditions or applicable legislation.

Advanced and/or qualified electronic signatures shall comply with Advanced Electronic Signatures (AdES Baseline Profiles) as included in the open standards list of the Netherlands Standardisation Forum.
Up-to-date records shall be kept of all Internet-facing information systems, web applications, IP addresses and APIs.
Publicly accessible websites shall be published via the Government Register of Internet Domains. This information shall be updated at least every six months.
Access to a trusted zone shall be permitted in two situations: 1. from authenticated devices, or 2. from software operating within a secure enclave.
A comprehensive formal registration and de-registration procedure shall be in place for the management of user identities.
The use of group accounts shall not be permitted unless motivated, recorded and coordinated with the CISO by the process owner.

Multi-factor authentication (MFA) shall, at a minimum, be applied for primary logon to the digital workplace, for accounts providing access to Internet-facing services, for accounts with administrative privileges and in other situations where the risk analysis indicates that this is an appropriate solution. These two forms of MFA shall be used: 1.  Passwordless access, such as a PIN in combination with a hardware token or a personally unique certificate (passkey). 2. Password-protected access combined with at least a second factor. If MFA is not possible for these accounts, other mitigating measures shall be taken. The CISO must be involved and the measures must be approved by the process owner. Where it is possible and safe to do so, MFA shall be combined with federative authentication tools such as Single Sign On and a Stepping Stone solution. For the management and monitoring of authentication data: − authentication information shall be issued only through formally established procedures and not until the user’s identity has been verified with sufficient assurance. − Use Cases for the misuse of authentication data shall be defined and monitored, and appropriate action shall be taken if such events occur. Such Use Cases include, at a minimum, login attempts from unusual locations and spikes in failed login attempts.
The organisation shall provide all employees access to a password manager or equivalent solution.
Enforcement of password requirements shall be automated.

The creation of and modifications to accounts with special privileges shall be monitored. If such a change is found to be unauthorised, this qualifies as a security incident and shall be recorded and handled accordingly.
All access rights issued shall be assessed at least once a year. A risk assessment shall be made to determine whether a higher frequency is required.

For requests for a proposal where information or information systems are involved, information security requirements (availability, integrity and confidentiality) shall be included as part of the complete set of procurement requirements. The information security requirements shall be based on an explicit risk assessment.
The security requirements arising from the request for a proposal shall be explicitly included in (procurement) contracts that involve information processing.

Where possible, the general terms and conditions of suppliers shall be explicitly excluded and where appropriate, additional conditions shall be included. If conditions cannot be excluded, an assessment shall be made of the associated risks. When entering into the agreement, it shall be explicitly defined which consequences are acceptable, which must be mitigated and which conditions will not or may never be accepted.

The procurement contract shall include a requirement for the supplier to demonstrate that it meets all specified requirements concerning set-up, existence and operation, based on assessments by independent third parties. The scope of those independent assessments shall cover the full range of the services under the contract. Explicit attention shall be given to the supply chain and how the supplier has organised its supplier management, in accordance with government measure 5.21.01. The supplier shall demonstrate this on an annual basis.

The government organisation shall conduct its own independent investigations, also to validate the reports provided by the supplier. To that end, the possibility to commission an external audit shall be explicitly included in the contract. The government organisation shall control any residual risks arising from the foregoing by applying its adopted risk management methodology.

The parties shall agree, among other things, that the supplier is transparent about the vulnerabilities in its services and about information security incidents, including data leaks. This enables the government organisation to respond appropriately, for example by reporting the incident and taking mitigating measures.

Before a contract is concluded, a risk assessment shall determine whether the dependency on a particular supplier is manageable. An explicit and detailed definition of the exit strategy shall be a standard component of the contract.
The contract shall stipulate that the supplier is responsible for ensuring compliance, by its subcontractors, with the specified requirements.

Before the contract is concluded, the supplier shall provide insight into the chain of subcontractors and any risks involved. The government organisation shall then assess whether those risks are acceptable.

The government organisation shall guarantee that the security requirements imposed on the supplier equally and fully apply to the chain of subcontractors, unless those requirements are not relevant in view of the nature of the supplier’s services.

During the term of the contract the supplier shall communicate changes in the chain of subcontractors, including the associated risks. At minimum, this shall cover vulnerabilities and information security incidents that can affect services to the government organisation.

Based on the evidence provided by the supplier, see government measure 5.20.03, the process owner shall be responsible for an annual assessment of the extent to which the supplier meets the information security requirements in place, for identifying any security risks, for taking or commissioning mitigating measures and for accepting residual risks.
An up-to-date register of suppliers and existing contracts shall be kept.

Policies shall be put in place that cover the identification, classification, selection, assessment and management of Cloud Service Providers (CSPs), as well as the termination of services provided by CSPs. Those policies shall be implemented and shall be reviewed at least once every three years. Each contract shall identify the situations that may give rise to its termination. In the event of major changes with the supplier, the associated risks shall be assessed and suitable measures shall be taken.
All internal and external employees shall have access to a low-threshold notification desk where they can report and register information security incidents.
The tasks and responsibilities of the notification desk shall be laid down in an incident reporting procedure.
The process owner shall be responsible for resolving information security incidents.
On a monthly basis, the process owner shall report on the follow-up of information security incidents to the person with ultimate responsibility for operations.
The procedure for information security incidents shall include a link to crisis management.

Supply chain security shall be included in the risk analysis for the organisation. The risk analysis shall include a focus on the following aspects: − specific vulnerabilities of each direct supplier and service provider; − the overall quality of the products; − the cybersecurity practices of their suppliers and service providers, including their secure development procedures.

The incident reporting procedure shall be designed to: − report information security incidents to the national Cyber Security Incident Response Team (CSIRT) within the statutory time limit; − receive and assess notifications from the national CSIRT and incorporate them into risk management; − inform the parties involved about the incident within the statutory time limit.

Information security incidents shall be handled via the incident management process. If relevant, such incidents shall be reported to regulatory authorities pursuant to the statutory provisions involved, such as the Cyber Security Act, the Public Records Act and the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).
Information security incidents shall be analysed in order to establish the root causes and realise improvements with the aim to prevent future incidents.
The information security incident analysis reports, including the root causes and improvements, shall be shared widely among relevant partners in order to prevent similar and future incidents.

The retention period for a (suspected) information security incident and all information required to analyse and resolve it shall be at least three years. This includes, among other things, the information required for the analysis (including logging), the resolution and recommendations.
Every year, the process owner shall test continuity plans for effectiveness, completeness and current relevance with a view to improving them.

As part of the inventory under control measure 5.12, the process owner shall identify critical systems on the basis of the established risk management methodology and an explicit risk assessment. The process owner shall update this overview at least once every three years.

The process owner shall have included the retention periods for all information and information systems in selection lists, with due regard for the organisation’s own objectives and for laws and regulations, such as the Public Records Act and privacy regulations. Additionally, the process owner shall have implemented these retention periods in practice and shall periodically test their effectiveness.
There shall be an operational ISMS in place in accordance with NEN-EN-ISO/IEC ISO 27001.
An established audit plan shall be in place, in which annual decisions are made regarding which systems will undergo which type of security audit.

Within the planning and control (P&C) cycle, and as part of the plan-do-check-act (PDCA) cycle, reporting on information security shall take place under the coordination of the CISO. This shall result in an annual In Control Statement (ICV), or a comparable instrument, covering the organisation’s entire information security system. The ICV or the comparable instrument can also be part of the formal accountability procedure.

Every organisation shall have its own established screening policy. Upon commencement of employment and in the event of a job change, a Certificate of Conduct (VOG) may be requested based on a risk assessment.

All internal and external employees, upon commencement of employment or in the event of a job change, shall have been made aware of their responsibilities for information security. They shall have easy access to the information security regulations and instructions that apply to them.

All employees, line managers and board members shall share responsibility for protecting business information. Everybody shall know the rules and obligations concerning information security and, where relevant, any special requirements for classified environments.
All employees and contractors who use the information systems and services shall have successfully completed an ‘I-awareness’ training course within three months after their appointment.

Upon appointment, internal transfer and, for example, during team meetings or performance reviews, management shall emphasise to its employees and contractors the importance of education and training in the field of information security. Management shall actively encourage them to periodically attend such training.
All internal and external employees shall have demonstrably taken note of the notification procedure for information security incidents.
Secure zones shall be set up based on standards.
Critical information or information systems shall never be accessible via a single secure zone.
In the event of specific security risks, warnings shall be sent, in accordance with mutual agreements, to the relevant colleagues within the government’s security domain.
When a chip card token is used for access to systems, the access security lock shall be automatically activated upon removal of the token.
A deletion instruction shall be in place pursuant to which any business-sensitive content on removable media that are reusable and leave the organisation shall have been irretrievably deleted.

For the purpose of erasing all data on the medium, data shall be irretrievably deleted or made inaccessible. A check shall be carried out to ensure that all data has been irretrievably deleted. A report shall be made of this.  Preferably, products shall be used for which the Resilience Unit of the National Communications Security Agency (NBV) has issued a positive deployment recommendation.
The use of couriers or forwarders for the transport of classified information shall meet predefined reliability requirements.

Mobile equipment shall be set up in such a way that business information is not stored on user devices as standard (‘zero footprint’). If a (near) zero footprint is not (yet) achievable, a mobile device (such as a laptop, tablet or smartphone) shall provide the option to protect access with an access security mechanism that includes, at a minimum, data encryption. Mobile equipment shall include ‘remote deletion’ functionality.

When mobile equipment is used, the following implementations shall have been effected, at a minimum: − Awareness-building programmes address behavioural aspects of safe mobile working. − The device is subject to patch management and hardening. − Mobile Device Management (MDM) or Mobile Application Management (MAM) solutions are used. − Users sign a mobile working agreement. By doing so, they acknowledge that they are aware of the risks of mobile working and declare that they will do so safely. This acknowledgement applies to all mobile devices that the employee uses for business purposes. Compliance with the provisions in sections 1., 2. and 3. shall be checked periodically.
The assigned or exercised special privileges shall be assessed at least on a quarterly basis in terms of their set-up, existence and operation.
Measures shall be in place to safeguard the physical and/or logical isolation of information of specific importance.
Users shall only be able to view and process the information of specific importance they need to perform their duties.

The granting of network access to external suppliers shall be preceded by a risk assessment to determine the conditions under which, and for how long, the suppliers are granted access. A register shall be kept to show how rights have been assigned.
The downloading of files shall be controlled and restricted based on risk and need-to-use. The antimalware software shall always screen all downloads.
Users shall have been informed about the risk of surfing behaviour and of clicking unknown links.
The antimalware software and associated recovery software shall be up to date and supported by periodic updates.

The malware scan shall be performed on: − all environments, such as (mail) servers, (desktop) computers and when granting access to the organisation’s network; − all downloaded content prior to execution or storage; − all files received via networks or any form of storage medium, before use or storage within the organisation’s own environment.

If both the likelihood of misuse and the expected damage are high (for example, according to the NCSC Escalation Matrix for Security Advice or supplier security recommendations), appropriate mitigating measures shall be implemented as quickly as possible, but no later than within one week.
How mitigating measures will be implemented shall be based on an explicit risk assessment.
In the meantime, or if installation cannot be realised within a week, mitigating measures shall be taken on the basis of an explicit risk assessment.

Information systems shall preferably undergo annual tests for technical compliance with security standards and actual safety risks, for example by means of (automated) vulnerability analyses, penetration tests or red-teaming tests. Internet-facing information systems shall be tested, preferably continuously, for weaknesses and vulnerabilities.

Internet-facing information systems shall undergo a mandatory (preferably automated) penetration test upon every new release or major update. If those tests identify any high-risk issues that cannot be mitigated in any other way, the system shall not be allowed to be taken into operation. All Internet-facing information systems shall be tested at least once a year for weaknesses and vulnerabilities.

A Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure (CVD) procedure shall be designed and published in accordance with the NCSC guideline or NEN-EN-ISO/IEC 29147:2020 Vulnerability disclosure. Information arising from Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure (CVD) reports shall be included in the incident report.

A backup policy shall be in place in which the requirements for retention and protection are defined and established. This shall include a special focus on protecting the back-up against ransomware attacks and on measures taken to preserve the integrity of the back-up.
The maximum permissible data loss and the maximum recovery time following an incident shall have been determined based on an explicit risk assessment.
The back-up process shall provide for the location-based storage of the back-up in such a way that an incident at one location cannot result in damage at another location.
The recovery procedure shall be tested at least annually or following a major change, to ensure its proper functioning in case of an emergency.

A log entry shall contain at a minimum: − Action: the event or operation that occurred. − Object: the item affected by the event or operation (for example, which file, process, or system). − Result: the result of the event or operation. − Origin: the device or network location from where the event or operation originated. − Actor: identification of the person who or the process that made the event happen. − Time stamp: the date and time at which the event or operation took place.
A log entry shall never contain data that could lead to a security breach.
There shall be a list of log files that are generated.

The retention period of log files and data in the Security Incident and Event Monitoring (SIEM) system shall be determined on the basis of risk, taking into account scenarios in which attackers remain undetected for an extended period.

Improper modification or deletion (or attempts thereof) of log data shall be reported as an information security incident as quickly as possible, following the information security incident procedure in accordance with control measure 5.24.

Based on an explicit risk assessment, the organisation shall determine the periodic verification of the integrity of log files throughout the retention period. The verification shall be carried out by an independent official (separate from operations).
Any new threats (attacks) discovered under government measure 8.16.3 shall be shared with the designated Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT) within the applicable legal framework.
The SIEM and/or SOC monitoring processes shall include clear rules about when to report an incident to the managers responsible.
The information processing environment shall be monitored using a detection and response solution that enables detection of attacks and an effective and timely response to any anomalous event.
Active network components shall include logging (and log monitoring) functionality in order to detect and respond to anomalous events.
Access to system utilities shall be restricted to authorised staff members, who shall only have access when strictly necessary.
The use of system utilities shall be logged. The logging data shall remain available for investigation for six months.
Controls must be in place to prevent users from installing non-authorised software.
At a minimum, network components shall comply with the confidentiality level of the network of which they form part.
Access to management interfaces of network components shall be separated from the user network (as far as possible and in a risk-based manner).

At connection points with external or untrusted zones, and due to network segmentation, measures shall have been implemented to detect and mitigate possible attacks that could adversely affect the availability of information, such as DDoS (Distributed Denial of Service) attacks.
Detection tools shall be in place to monitor/analyse data traffic to and from the trusted environment for the presence of any suspicious traffic.
Any new threats identified under government measure 8.21.02 shall be passed on and shared within the government, with due regard for the applicable legal frameworks.

When data are transmitted over wireless connections such as Wi-Fi and over wired connections outside the controlled area, the data shall be encrypted, with the exception of metadata that are necessary to establish the transmission. The configuration of the encryption shall be risk-based and shall take into account the required duration and level of protection. Preferably, encryption tools shall be used for which the Resilience Unit of the General Intelligence and Security Service (AIVD) has issued a positive deployment recommendation. If the Resilience Unit does not have any recommended encryption tools, a different encryption method shall be selected and set up in consultation with the CISO.
Each segregated group shall have its own security level.

The cryptography policy shall cover at least the following topics: − when cryptography is used; − who is responsible for implementation; − who is responsible for key management; − how it is recorded which cryptography is applied, and where; − which standards serve as the basis for cryptography and how the standards of the Netherlands Standardisation Forum are applied; − how the level of protection is established. − In communication between organisations, the policy shall be determined in mutual consultation.

Cryptographic control measures shall be included in the inventory of business assets. For all cryptographic control measures it shall be established where they are used, who is responsible for them and how they are kept up to date.
Cryptographic control measures shall comply with the relevant standards of the Netherlands Standardisation Forum.
The strength of the cryptography shall be based on the current recommendations of the NCSC and the AIVD Resilience Unit.

There shall be (contractual) agreements on backup certificates from an alternative supplier if the risk assessment shows that these are necessary as part of business continuity readiness (control measure 5.30).

Architectural principles such as ‘security by design’ and ‘security by default’ for the security design of information systems shall be adopted, documented, maintained and applied for all activities involved in the development of information systems.
Structured test methodologies shall be used for system acceptance testing. The tests shall preferably be carried out in an automated manner. The results of the tests shall be included in a report.
Internal measures for system development shall apply in full to outsourced development, supplemented with the measures arising from outsourcing.
No tests shall be carried out in the production environment. Departures from this rule shall be permitted only with the prior approval of the process owner.

Significant changes in the production environment shall always be tested before being put into production. Departures from this rule shall be permitted only with the prior approval of the process owner.

At a minimum, the change management process shall focus on: − the administration of changes, including the results of the test plan; − a risk assessment of the potential consequences of the changes, including a written roll-back plan; − the approval procedure for changes.
Change management shall be conducted on the basis of a generally accepted management framework.
[KEY MEASURE] The activity logging functionality of protection / detection hardware or software  (e.g. firewalls, anti-virus) shall be enabled, backed-up and reviewed.
Firewalls shall be installed and  operated on the network boundaries and completed with firewall protection on the endpoints.
End point and network protection tools to monitor end-user behavior for dangerous activity shall be implemented.
[KEY MEASURE] Anti-virus, -spyware, and other -malware programs shall be installed and updated.
An inventory of assets associated with information and information processing facilities within the organization shall be documented, reviewed, and updated when changes occur.
An inventory that reflects what software platforms and applications are being used in the organization shall be documented, reviewed, and updated when changes occur.
Information that the organization stores and uses shall be identified.
The organization’s resources (hardware, devices, data, time, personnel, information, and software) shall be prioritized based on their classification, criticality, and business value.
Policies and procedures for information security and cyber security shall be created, documented, reviewed, approved, and updated when changes occur.
Legal and regulatory requirements regarding information/cybersecurity, including privacy obligations, shall be understood and implemented.
As part of the company's overall risk management, a comprehensive strategy to manage information security and cybersecurity risks shall be developed and updated when changes occur.
Threats and vulnerabilities shall be identified.
The organization shall conduct risk assessments in which risk is determined by threats, vulnerabilities and impact on business processes and assets.
[KEY MEASURE] Identities and credentials for authorized devices and users shall be managed.
Physical access to the facility, servers and network components shall be managed.
The organisation's wireless access points shall be secured.
[KEY MEASURE] The organization's networks when accessed remotely shall be secured, including through multi-factor authentication (MFA).
[KEY MEASURE] Access permissions for users to the organization’s systems shall be defined and managed.
[KEY MEASURE] It shall be identified who should have access to the organization's business's critical information and technology and the means to get access.
[KEY MEASURE] Employee access to data and information shall be limited to the systems and specific information they need to do their jobs (the principle of Least Privilege).
[KEY MEASURE] Nobody shall have administrator privileges for daily tasks.
[KEY MEASURE] Firewalls shall be installed and activated on all the organization's networks.
[KEY MEASURE] Where appropriate, network integrity of the organization's critical systems shall be protected by incorporating network segmentation and segregation.
Employees shall be trained as appropriate.
Assets and media shall be disposed of safely.
Personnel having access to the organization’s most critical information or technology shall be verified.
[KEY MEASURE] Backups for organization's business critical data shall be conducted and stored on a system different from the device on which the original data resides
[KEY MEASURE] Patches and security updates for Operating Systems and critical system components shall be installed.
[KEY MEASURE]  Logs shall be maintained, documented, and reviewed.
Web and e-mail filters shall be installed and used.
A recovery process for disasters and information/cybersecurity incidents shall be developed and executed as appropriate.
Information/cybersecurity incident information shall be communicated and shared with the organization’s employees in a format that they can understand.

The organization shall conduct post-incident evaluations to analyse lessons learned from incident response and recovery, and consequently improve processes / procedures / technologies to enhance its cyber resilience.
An incident response process, including roles, responsibilities, and authorities, shall be executed during or after an information/cybersecurity event on the organization's critical systems.
Anomalous activity is detected and the potential impact of events is understood.
A baseline of network operations and expected data flows for users and systems is established and managed
[KEY MEASURE] The organization shall ensure that a baseline of network operations and expected data flows for its critical systems is developed, documented and maintained to track events.
Detected events are analyzed to understand attack targets and methods
The organization shall implement automated mechanisms where feasible to review and analyze detected events.
Event data are collected and correlated from multiple sources and sensors

The organization shall integrate analysis of events where feasible with the analysis of vulnerability scanning information; performance data; its critical system's monitoring, and facility monitoring to further enhance the ability to identify inappropriate or unusual activity.
Impact of events is determined
Negative impacts to organization’s operations, assets, and individuals resulting from detected events shall be determined and correlated with risk assessment outcomes.
Incident alert thresholds are established
The information system and assets are monitored to identify cybersecurity events and verify the effectiveness of protective measures.
The network is monitored to detect potential cybersecurity events
The organization shall conduct ongoing security status monitoring of its network to detect defined information/cybersecurity events and indicators of potential information/cybersecurity events.
The physical environment is monitored to detect potential cybersecurity events

The physical access to organization's critical systems and devices shall be, on top of the physical access monitoring to the facility, increased through physical intrusion alarms, surveillance equipment, independent surveillance teams.
Personnel activity is monitored to detect potential cybersecurity events
Malicious code is detected
The organisation shall set up a system to detect false positives while detecting and eradicating malicious code.
Unauthorized mobile code is detected
External service provider activity is monitored to detect potential cybersecurity events
Monitoring for unauthorized personnel, connections, devices, and software is performed
Unauthorized configuration changes to organization's systems shall be monitored and addressed with the appropriate mitigation actions.
Vulnerability scans are performed
Detection processes and procedures are maintained and tested to ensure awareness of anomalous events.
Detection activities comply with all applicable requirements
Detection processes are tested
Event detection information is communicated
Detection processes are continuously improved

The organization shall conduct specialized assessments including in-depth monitoring, vulnerability scanning, malicious user testing, insider threat assessment, performance/load testing, and verification and validation testing on the organization's critical systems.

The data, personnel, devices, systems, and facilities that enable the organization to achieve business purposes are identified and managed consistent with their relative importance to organizational objectives and the organization’s risk strategy.
Physical devices and systems within the organization are inventoried
Mechanisms for detecting the presence of unauthorized hardware and firmware components within the organization's network shall be identified.
Software platforms and applications within the organization are inventoried
Mechanisms for detecting the presence of unauthorized software within the organization’s ICT/OT environment shall be identified.
Organizational communication and data flows are mapped

The information flows/data flows within the organization’s ICT/OT environment, as well as to other organization-internal systems shall be mapped, documented, authorized, and updated when changes occur.
External information systems are catalogued
The flow of information to/from external systems shall be mapped, documented, authorized, and update when changes occur.
Resources (e.g., hardware, devices, data, time, personnel, and software) are prioritized based on their classification, criticality, and business value
Cybersecurity roles, responsibilities, and authorities for the entire workforce and third-party stakeholders are established
The organization shall appoint an information security officer.

The organization’s mission, objectives, stakeholders, and activities are understood and prioritized; this information is used to inform cybersecurity roles, responsibilities, and risk management decisions.
The organization’s role in the supply chain is identified and communicated
The organization shall protect its ICT/OT environment from supply chain threats by applying security safeguards as part of a documented comprehensive security strategy.
The organization’s place in critical infrastructure and its industry sector is identified and communicated
Priorities for organizational mission, objectives, and activities are established and communicated
Dependencies and critical functions for delivery of critical services are established
Resilience requirements to support delivery of critical services are established for all operating states (e.g. under duress/attack, during recovery, normal operations)
Information processing & supporting facilities shall implement redundancy to meet availability requirements, as defined by the organization and/or regulatory frameworks.
Recovery time and recovery point objectives for the resumption of essential ICT/OT system processes shall be defined.

The policies, procedures, and processes to manage and monitor the organization’s regulatory, legal, risk, environmental, and operational requirements are understood and inform the management of cybersecurity risk.
Organizational cybersecurity policy is established and communicated
Legal and regulatory requirements regarding cybersecurity, including privacy and civil liberties obligations, are understood and managed
Governance and risk management processes address cybersecurity risks
The organization understands the cybersecurity risk to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational assets, and individuals.
Asset vulnerabilities are identified and documented

To ensure that organization's operations are not adversely impacted by the testing process, performance/load testing and penetration testing on the organization’s systems shall be conducted with care.
Cyber threat intelligence is received from information sharing forums and sources
It shall be identified where automated mechanisms can be implemented to make security alert and advisory information available to relevant organization stakeholders.
Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to determine risk
Risk assessment results shall be disseminated to relevant stakeholders.
Risk responses are identified and prioritized
The organization’s priorities, constraints, risk tolerances, and assumptions are established and used to support operational risk decisions.
Risk management processes are established, managed, and agreed to by organizational stakeholders
Organizational risk tolerance is determined and clearly expressed
The organization’s determination of risk tolerance is informed by its role in critical infrastructure and sector specific risk analysis

The organization’s priorities, constraints, risk tolerances, and assumptions are established and used to support risk decisions associated with managing supply chain risk. The organization has established and implemented the processes to identify, assess and manage supply chain risks.
Cyber supply chain risk management processes are identified, established, assessed, managed, and agreed to by organizational stakeholders

The organization shall document, review, approve, update when changes occur, and implement a cyber supply chain risk management process that supports the identification, assessment, and mitigation of the risks associated with the distributed and interconnected nature of ICT/OT product and service supply chains.
Suppliers and third party partners of information systems, components, and services are identified, prioritized, and assessed using a cyber supply chain risk assessment process
A documented list of all the organization’s suppliers, vendors and partners who may be involved in a major incident shall be established, kept up-to-date and made available online and offline.

Contracts with suppliers and third-party partners are used to implement appropriate measures designed to meet the objectives of an organization’s cybersecurity program and Cyber Supply Chain Risk Management Plan.

[KEY MEASURE] Contractual information security and cybersecurity’ requirements for suppliers and third-party partners shall be implemented to ensure a verifiable flaw remediation process, and to ensure the correction of flaws identified during ‘information security and cybersecurity’ testing and evaluation.

[KEY MEASURE] The organization shall establish contractual requirements permitting the organization to review the ‘information security and cybersecurity’ programs implemented by suppliers and third-party partners.
Suppliers and third-party partners are routinely assessed using audits, test results, or other forms of evaluations to confirm they are meeting their contractual obligations.

The organization shall review assessments of suppliers’ and third-party partner’s compliance with contractual obligations by routinely reviewing third-party independent audits, test results, and other evaluations.
Response and recovery planning and testing are conducted with suppliers and third-party providers
The organization shall identify and document key personnel from suppliers and third-party partners to include them as stakeholders in testing and execution of the response and recovery plans.
The organization shall review and analyze detected events to understand attack targets and methods.

The organization shall ensure that event data is compiled and correlated across its critical systems using various sources such as event reports, audit monitoring, network monitoring, physical access monitoring, and user/administrator reports.
The organization shall implement automated mechanisms and system generated alerts to support event detection and to assist in the identification of security alert thresholds.
The organization shall define incident alert thresholds.

[KEY MEASURE] The organization shall monitor and identify unauthorized use of its business critical systems through the detection of unauthorized local connections, network connections and remote connections.
The physical environment of the facility shall be monitored for potential information/cybersecurity events.
End point and network protection tools that monitor end-user behavior for dangerous activity shall be managed.
Software usage and installation restrictions shall be enforced.
The organization shall define acceptable and unacceptable mobile code and mobile code technologies; and authorize, monitor, and control the use of mobile code within the system.
All external connections by vendors supporting IT/OT applications or infrastructure shall be secured and actively monitored to ensure that only permissible actions occur during the connection.
External service providers' conformance with personnel security policies and procedures and contract security requirements shall be monitored relative to their cybersecurity risks.
The organization's business critical systems shall be monitored for unauthorized personnel access, connections, devices, access points, and software.
The organization shall monitor and scan for vulnerabilities in its critical systems and hosted applications ensuring that system functions are not adversely impacted by the scanning process.
The vulnerability scanning process shall include analysis, remediation, and information sharing.
The organization shall conduct detection activities in accordance with applicable federal and regional laws, industry regulations and standards, policies, and other applicable requirements.
The organization shall validate that event detection processes are operating as intended.
The organization shall communicate event detection information to predefined parties.
Improvements derived from the monitoring, measurement, assessment, testing, review, and lessons learned, shall be incorporated into detection process revisions.

The inventory of assets associated with information and information processing facilities shall reflect changes in the  organization’s context and include all information necessary for effective accountability.
When unauthorized hardware is detected, it shall be quarantined for possible exception handling, removed, or replaced, and the inventory shall be updated accordingly.

The inventory of software platforms and applications  associated with information and information processing shall reflect changes in the  organization’s context and include all information necessary for effective accountability.
Individuals who are responsible and who are accountable for administering software platforms and applications within the organization shall be identified.
When unauthorized software is detected, it shall be quarantined for possible exception handling, removed, or replaced, and the inventory shall be updated accordingly.
All connections within the organization's ICT/OT environment, and to other organization-internal platforms shall be mapped, documented, approved, and updated as appropriate.
The organization shall map, document, authorize and when changes occur, update, all external services and the connections made with them.

[KEY MEASURE] Information security and cybersecurity roles, responsibilities and authorities within the organization shall be documented, reviewed, authorized, and updated and alignment with organization-internal roles and external partners.
The organization’s role in the supply chain shall be identified, documented, and communicated.
The organization’s place in critical infrastructure and its industry sector shall be identified and communicated.
Priorities for organizational mission, objectives, and activities are established and communicated.

Dependencies and mission-critical functions for the delivery of critical services shall be identified, documented, and prioritized according to their criticality as part of the risk assessment process.
To support cyber resilience and secure the delivery of critical services, the necessary requirements are identified, documented and their implementation tested and approved.
An organization-wide information security and cybersecurity policy shall be established, documented, updated when changes occur, disseminated, and approved by senior management.
Legal and regulatory requirements regarding information/cybersecurity, including privacy obligations, shall be managed.
Information security and cybersecurity risks shall be documented, formally approved, and updated when changes occur.
A process shall be established to monitor, identify, and document vulnerabilities of the organisation's business critical systems in a continuous manner.
A threat and vulnerability awareness program that includes a cross-organization information-sharing capability shall be implemented.
The organization shall conduct and  document risk assessments in which risk is determined by threats, vulnerabilities, impact on business processes and assets, and the likelihood of their occurrence.
A comprehensive strategy shall be developed and implemented to manage risks to the organization’s critical systems, that includes the identification and prioritization of risk responses.

A cyber risk management process that identifies key internal and external stakeholders and facilitates addressing risk-related issues and information shall be created, documented, reviewed, approved, and updated when changes occur.
The organization shall clearly determine it’s risk appetite.
The organization’s role in critical infrastructure and its sector shall determine the organization’s risk appetite.

The organization shall conduct cyber supply chain risk assessments at least annually or when a change to the organization’s critical systems, operational environment, or supply chain occurs; These assessments shall be documented, and the results disseminated to relevant stakeholders including those responsible for ICT/OT systems.

Based on the results of the cyber supply chain risk assessment, a contractual framework for suppliers and external partners shall be established to address sharing of sensitive information and distributed and interconnected ICT/OT products and services.
The organization shall review assessments of suppliers’ and third-party partner’s compliance with contractual obligations by routinely reviewing audits, test results, and other evaluations.
The organization shall identify and document key personnel from suppliers and third-party partners to include them as stakeholders in response and recovery planning activities.
Identities and credentials for authorized devices and users shall be managed, where feasible through automated mechanisms.
The management of physical access shall include measures related to access in emergency situations.

[KEY MEASURE] Usage restrictions, connection requirements, implementation guidance, and authorizations for remote access to the organization’s critical systems environment shall be identified, documented and implemented.

Provide security awareness training on recognizing and reporting potential indicators of insider threat. • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.2.3

Create and retain system audit logs and records to the extent needed to enable the monitoring, analysis, investigation, and reporting of unlawful or unauthorized system activity.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.3.1
Ensure that the actions of individual system users can be uniquely traced to those users, so they can be held accountable for their actions.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.3.2
Review and update logged events. • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.3.3
Alert in the event of an audit logging process failure.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.3.4

Correlate audit record review, analysis, and reporting processes for investigation and response to indications of unlawful, unauthorized, suspicious, or unusual activity. • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.3.5
Provide audit record reduction and report generation to support on-demand analysis and reporting. • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.3.6
Provide a system capability that compares and synchronizes internal system clocks with an authoritative source to generate time stamps for audit records. • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.3.7
Protect audit information and audit logging tools from unauthorized access, modification, and deletion. • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.3.8
Limit management of audit logging functionality to a subset of privileged users.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.3.9
Periodically assess the security controls in organizational systems to determine if the controls are effective in their application.   • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.12.1
Develop and implement plans of action designed to correct deficiencies and reduce or eliminate vulnerabilities in organizational systems. • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.12.2
Monitor security controls on an ongoing basis to ensure the continued effectiveness of the controls.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.12.3

Develop, document, and periodically update system security plans that describe system boundaries, system environments of operation, how security requirements are implemented, and the relationships with or connections to other systems.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.12.4

Establish and maintain baseline configurations and inventories of organizational systems (including hardware, software, firmware, and documentation) throughout the respective system development life cycles. • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.4.1
Establish and enforce security configuration settings for information technology products employed in organizational systems. • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.4.2
Track, review, approve or disapprove, and log changes to organizational systems.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.4.3
Analyze the security impact of changes prior to implementation.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.4.4
Define, document, approve, and enforce physical and logical access restrictions associated with changes to organizational systems.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.4.5
Employ the principle of least functionality by configuring organizational systems to provide only essential capabilities.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.4.6
Restrict, disable, or prevent the use of nonessential programs, functions, ports, protocols, and services.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.4.7

Apply deny-by-exception (blacklisting) policy to prevent the use of unauthorized software or deny-all, permit-by-exception (whitelisting) policy to allow the execution of authorized software.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.4.8
Control and monitor user-installed software. • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.4.9
Identify information system users, processes acting on behalf of users, or devices. • FAR Clause 52.204-21 b.1.v • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.5.1

Authenticate (or verify) the identities of those users, processes, or devices, as a prerequisite to allowing access to organizational information systems. • FAR Clause 52.204-21 b.1.vi • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.5.2
Store and transmit only cryptographically-protected passwords.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.5.10
Obscure feedback of authentication information.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.5.11
Use multifactor authentication for local and network access to privileged accounts and for network access to non-privileged accounts.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.5.3
Employ replay-resistant authentication mechanisms for network access to privileged and non-privileged accounts. • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.5.4
Prevent reuse of identifiers for a defined period.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.5.5
Disable identifiers after a defined period of inactivity.   • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.5.6
Enforce a minimum password complexity and change of characters when new passwords are created. • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.5.7
Prohibit password reuse for a specified number of generations.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.5.8
Allow temporary password use for system logons with an immediate change to a permanent password.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.5.9

Establish an operational incident-handling capability for organizational systems that includes preparation, detection, analysis, containment, recovery, and user response activities. • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.6.1
Track, document, and report incidents to designated officials and/or authorities both internal and external to the organization. • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.6.2
Test the organizational incident response capability. • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.6.3

Provide controls on the tools, techniques, mechanisms, and personnel used to conduct system maintenance. • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.7.2

Control the use of removable media on system components. • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.8.7
Prohibit the use of portable storage devices when such devices have no identifiable owner. • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.8.8
Protect the confidentiality of backup CUI at storage locations.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.8.9

Limit physical access to organizational information systems, equipment, and the respective operating environments to authorized individuals.  • FAR Clause 52.204-21 b.1.viii • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.10.1
Escort visitors and monitor visitor activity.  • FAR Clause 52.204-21 Partial b.1.ix  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.10.3
Maintain audit logs of physical access. • FAR Clause 52.204-21 Partial b.1.ix  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.10.4
Control and manage physical access devices. • FAR Clause 52.204-21 Partial b.1.ix  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.10.5
Protect and monitor the physical facility and support infrastructure for organizational systems. • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.10.2
Enforce safeguarding measures for CUI at alternate work sites.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.10.6
Screen individuals prior to authorizing access to organizational systems containing CUI. • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.9.1
Ensure that organizational systems containing CUI are protected during and after personnel actions such as terminations and transfers.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.9.2

Periodically assess the risk to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational assets, and individuals, resulting from the operation of organizational systems and the associated processing, storage, or transmission of CUI. • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.11.1

Implement subnetworks for publicly accessible system components that are physically or logically separated from internal networks. • FAR Clause 52.204-21 b.1.xi • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.13.5

Prohibit remote activation of collaborative computing devices and provide indication of devices in use to users present at the device.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.13.12
Control and monitor the use of mobile code.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.13.13
Control and monitor the use of Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) technologies. • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.13.14
Protect the authenticity of communications sessions. • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.13.15
Protect the confidentiality of CUI at rest. • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.13.16

Monitor organizational systems, including inbound and outbound communications traffic, to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.14.6
Identify unauthorized use of organizational systems.  • NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 3.14.7
