Coordinate with other organizational plans (CP-2(1)).    Identify critical assets to prioritize in the event of a crisis (CP-2(8

Train OT staff on contingency procedures.       Organize training sessions for OT operators on incident management.    Conduct regular testing and assessments of employees' knowledge of business continuity.    Develop guides and manuals for quick reference during crises

Conduct tests and exercises of the contingency plan to ensure its effectiveness.       Conduct annual contingency plan tests (CP-4(1)).    Conduct real-world exercises to identify flaws in the plan.    Document lessons learned after each test and incorporate them into the updated plan.

Provide a secondary storage site for critical data and equipment.       Identify a secure remote site to store backups and critical equipment.    Ensure connectivity and quick access to stored data and systems in the event of a crisis.    Regularly test access to backups to avoid errors during recovery

Provide a secondary site to ensure business continuity in the event of a primary site outage.       Establish a secondary infrastructure that can take over in the event of a major incident.    Define protocols for automatic or semi-automatic failover to the alternative site.    Regularly test the passage to the emergency site to ensure that it is working properly.

Ensure critical communication services remain functional in the event of a disaster.       Have alternative telecommunications providers in the event of a main network outage.    Establish redundant communication networks, such as satellite links or dedicated mobile networks.    Test the resilience of communication infrastructures in the face of outages or attacks.

Perform regular and secure backups of OT systems and configurations.       Define an automated backup policy with a frequency adapted to OT needs.    Store local and offsite copies to prevent loss in the event of an attack or failure.    Regularly test backup restoration to ensure integrity

Establishes policies and procedures for managing identification and authentication in an OT environment.       Define clear roles and responsibilities for identity and authentication management.   Document processes for accessing OT systems.   Train staff on best practices in identity management.

Requires re-authentication after a period of inactivity or during sensitive actions.      Enforce re-authentication after a certain session time.   Require re-authentication to access certain critical resources.
Verifies users' identities before they register.      Implement multi-step identity verification procedures.   Require documentary proof of identity before the credentials are issued.

Ensures that only authorized users can access OT systems.      Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) for sensitive accounts.   Restrict the use of shared accounts and enforce strict access policies.   Use strong authentication methods such as smart cards or tokens.
Require MFA for manager accounts.
Accept secure identification cards (e.g. PIV cards) when applicable.
Extend MFA to standard users.
Allow individual authentication while allowing group authentication under certain conditions.
Prevent replay attacks via cryptographic mechanisms.

Ensures that devices connecting to OT systems are authenticated.      Implement authentication of OT devices before they can communicate.   Use digital certificates for device authentication.   Enforce strict asset identity management.
Two-way authentication via cryptography.
Verify the integrity of devices before they are connected.

Manage user and system credentials.      Assign unique identifiers to each user and device.   Implement restrictions on the reuse of credentials.   Differentiate identifiers according to access levels.
Indicate the status of users (e.g. employees, contractors, visitors).

Management of authentication mechanisms used to protect access to systems.       Enforce robust password management policies (length, complexity, rotation).   Prefer certificate-based authentication rather than passwords alone.   Restrict the transmission of plaintext passwords over the network.
Enforce strict password policies.
Use of public key authentication.
Protects authentication means from compromise.
Restricts the display of authentication information to prevent accidental leaks.      Hide on-screen password entries.   Prevent reuse of authentication responses

Verifies the authenticity of the cryptographic modules used.      Ensure that cryptographic modules are certified and compliant with standards (e.g. FIPS 140-3).   Restrict access to cryptographic modules to authorized users.
Manage authentication of external users accessing OT systems.      Implement specific controls for third-party access.   Require MFA for external connections.
Accept PIV cards from other agencies.
Accept third-party authenticators.
Apply standardized authentication profiles.

Establish a clear policy and procedures for incident management.      Define EO-specific procedures for responding to incidents.   Ensure alignment with IT and cybersecurity policies.   Train OT staff on incident response requirements.

Training of staff on best practices in incident response.   Organize regular training sessions for OT teams.   Conduct simulated incidents (IR-2(1)).   Deploy automated training environments (IR-2(2)).

Test the ability of systems and teams to respond to incidents.      Conduct hands-on incident management exercises.   Coordinate these tests with other plans (continuity, disaster recovery) (IR-3(2)).   Analyze results and improve procedures

Manage incidents in real time to limit their impact.      Implement automation processes (IR-4(1)).   Correlate incident information to other sources for better analysis (IR-4(4)).   Integrate an OT Incident Response Team (IR-4(11)).   Collaborate with vendors and partners to manage embedded component incidents.

Actively monitor for security incidents.      Deploy automated incident collection and analysis tools (IR-5(1)).   Continuously monitor OT systems and identify anomalies.   Set up automated alerts for critical incidents

Formalize incident reporting to internal and external stakeholders.      Ensure rapid escalation of incidents to the teams concerned.   Automate reporting for efficiency (IR-6(1)).   Coordinating reports with the supply chain and partners (IR-6(3)).   Collaborate with international organizations and CERTs (Cyber Emergency Response Teams).

Provide support to assist OT teams with incident management.      Set up a help desk for OT incidents.   Automate information management and resource availability (IR-7(1)).   Develop a network of partners specialized in OT incident response.

Develop a detailed plan to organize incident response.      Define the roles and responsibilities of staff.   Create an incident response workflow.   Integrate a classification of incidents based on their OT impact.   Document internal and external contacts to be notified in the event of an incident

Defines maintenance policies and procedures specific to OT environments.    Tailors these policies to the unique needs of industrial systems.       Write and maintain documented procedures for the maintenance of OT equipment.    Integrate cybersecurity requirements into maintenance policies.    Train maintenance personnel on the cybersecurity risks associated with interventions.

Ensures that equipment maintenance is planned, authorized, and tracked.    Preserves the integrity and safety of OT components during interventions.       Implement a process for validating maintenance interventions.    Document each intervention in a secure maintenance log.    Verify the integrity of systems after each maintenance operation

Controls the use of maintenance tools to avoid the risk of compromise.    Includes monitoring of storage media and external devices used during interventions.       Restrict the use of unapproved maintenance tools.    Check and sanitize tools before connecting them to OT systems.    Apply measures to protect against copying and exfiltration of data on external media.

Manages maintenance interventions carried out remotely via secure connections.    Implements mechanisms for monitoring and tracing remote access.       Use secure connections for any remote maintenance (VPN, strong authentication).    Record and audit all remote maintenance sessions (logs and captures).    Define procedures for automatic access shut-off after the intervention

Ensures that only authorized individuals can perform maintenance on OT systems.    Involves background checks and assigning specific permissions.       Implement a clearance control process for maintenance technicians.    Limit access to only necessary equipment based on the operator's role.    Conduct regular security checks on maintenance personnel

Ensures that maintenance operations are carried out in a timely manner to avoid critical failures.    Prevents failures through preventive maintenance programs.       Establish a preventive maintenance schedule to avoid unexpected interruptions.    Use monitoring sensors to detect anomalies before the outage.    Prioritize maintenance of critical components to avoid security risks.

Manages maintenance interventions carried out directly in the field (off-site).    Involves specific precautions for sensitive or critical OT equipment.       Identify systems that require special calibration or controlled maintenance.    Restrict maintenance to qualified people with specific tools.    Verify the compliance of interventions with regulatory and industrial standards.

Establishes policies and procedures to manage and protect media containing sensitive information, including those in OT environments.      Define a specific policy for the management of OT storage media.   Identify the special requirements related to OT-IT interactions.   Ensure that these procedures are regularly updated according to risks and emerging threats.

Controls access to physical and digital media to prevent unauthorized access.      Restrict access to media to authorized users only.   Implement authentication checks before use.   Regularly audit access for anomalies

Ensures that media containing sensitive information is properly labeled to prevent data leakage and mismanagement.      Clearly label all media containing critical information.   Use appropriate security classifications for OT media.   Train staff on the importance of marking and safe handling of media.

Defines measures to securely store physical and digital media to prevent unauthorized access or alteration.      Store sensitive media in secure areas with restricted access.   Use safes or locked cabinets for critical media.   Control and log access to physical and digital media

Establishes secure transport protocols to prevent data exposure when moving media.      Encrypt the data stored on the media being transported.   Use secure means of transport with supervision (e.g. authorised personnel, secure transport chains).   Establish procedures for tracking media in transit

Ensures that media is properly cleaned or destroyed before disposal or reuse to prevent unauthorized data recovery.      Apply standards-compliant data suppression methods (e.g., NIST SP 800-88).   Check that the media is effectively disinfected before they are recycled.   Document all media destruction procedures.

Sets restrictions on media usage to prevent data leakage and malware infections.      Prohibit the use of unauthorized removable media on OT systems.   Implement tools to control and log access to media.   Train employees on the risks of inappropriate media use.

Defines policies and procedures for the physical and environmental protection of OT systems. This includes regulatory aspects and EO-specific requirements.       Establish physical security policies that are appropriate for OT systems.    Develop documented procedures for physical access, monitoring, and infrastructure management.    Ensure regulatory compliance with applicable laws and standards

Allows for the emergency shutdown of certain critical OT systems in the event of an incident.       Implement emergency shutdown procedures.    Test the emergency stop buttons regularly.    Ensure that the emergency stop does not cause additional danger.
Manages backup power for critical OT systems.    Install backup UPS and generators.    Test the automatic failover capability regularly.    Ensure redundant power to prevent critical failures

Provides emergency lighting in the event of a power outage.       Install stand-alone emergency lights.    Periodically check the capacity of the batteries.    Ensure critical areas remain visible in the event of an incident

Protects OT installations from fire hazards.       Install smoke detectors and sprinklers.    Ensure that fire suppression systems are suitable for OT environments (avoid water in certain areas).    Conduct regular testing of firefighting equipment

Manages temperature, humidity and other environmental parameters.       Install HVAC systems suitable for OT infrastructures.    Monitor environmental conditions in real-time.    Use equipment that is designed to withstand extreme conditions.

Prevents water damage to OT equipment.       Install leak sensors and automatic shut-off valves.    Ensure that wiring and equipment are protected from water.    Regularly test drainage and drainage systems.

Manages physical access authorization to areas containing critical OT equipment.       Set up an allowlist to restrict access to OT areas.    Use access badges and biometric systems to identify authorized users.    Ensure regular review of access to remove obsolete permissions.

Implements physical controls to restrict and monitor access to OT facilities.       Install physical barriers (secure gates, fences, etc.).    Deploy surveillance cameras and alarms.    Enforce strict access control in case of emergency to ensure the safety of critical equipment.
Monitors physical access to OT systems and infrastructure.       Use intrusion sensors and alarms.    Provide real-time video monitoring.    Maintain an I/O history for incident analysis

Records visitor access to sensitive areas.       Maintain a visitor log with identity and reason for visit.    Supervise visits by authorized personnel.    Restricting access to critical areas to employees only

Secures electrical equipment and wiring from damage and sabotage.       Use cable trays that are secure and protected from interference.    Establish restricted areas for access to electrical equipment.    Monitor the temperature and health of power systems

This control requires the establishment of security policies and procedures that are appropriate for OT environments and how they interact with non-OT systems.       Draft and approve a security policy specific to OTs.    Define roles and responsibilities for OT cybersecurity management.    Establish a process for updating and revising policies based on technological developments and threats.

Select an appropriate security baseline based on OT risks and constraints.       Define minimum security standards for OT equipment and infrastructure.    Implement selection criteria for OT suppliers and equipment.    Perform compliance analyses to validate the implementation of baselines.

Develop and maintain a security and privacy plan for OT systems, to ensure consistency in risk management.       Develop an OT security planning document outlining the security controls and measures in place.    Integrate specific risk management scenarios into critical OT systems.    Achieve inter-system coordination to prevent a low-impact system from compromising a high-impact system

Define rules of behavior to be followed to ensure the secure use of OT systems.       Establish a clear access and usage policy for OT users.    Train operators in good cybersecurity practices.    Raise awareness of the risks of non-compliant actions, such as installing unauthorized software.

Document known operational procedures and analyze their relationship with IT and OT technologies.       Write a reference document detailing OT business processes.    Identify critical interdependencies between IT and OT.    Implement an OT incident response guide based on existing procedures.

Establish a robust security and privacy architecture for OT systems.       Implement a "Defense in Depth" approach.    Segment OT networks to limit the spread of attacks.    Integrate encryption and authentication controls adapted to OT constraints.

Centrally manage OT security, including breach remediation, malware protection, and event logging.       Implement a centralized OT vulnerability management platform.    Automate security log monitoring and anomaly detection.    Manage organization-wide security updates.

Control Name: Organization-Wide Information Security Program Management Controls

Control Description: The information security program plan defines the structure, objectives, resources, and responsibilities to ensure the ongoing management of cyber security.       Develop and document an information security plan covering all OT and IT systems.    Define cybersecurity roles and responsibilities.    Establish a process for evaluating and regularly updating the plan.    Coordinate with other organizational initiatives (risk management, safety, regulatory compliance).

Refers to a manager or team responsible for leading and managing the information security program.       Appoint a cybersecurity program manager (e.g., CISO, OT manager).    Clearly define their responsibilities and authority.    Coordinate with other stakeholders in the organization.

Ensure the availability of the necessary resources (human, financial and technological) for the implementation of the security program.       Allocate a specific budget to OT cybersecurity.    Identify and train qualified personnel in industrial cybersecurity.    Implement tools and technologies for monitoring and protecting OT systems.

Control Name: Plan of Action and Milestones Process
Control Description: Defines a formal process for identifying, tracking, and resolving cybersecurity gaps.       Establish a register of risks and corrective actions.    Assign responsibilities and timelines for each action.    Ensure regular follow-up and updates of action plans

Maintain an accurate inventory of information systems and OT equipment.       Document all OT and IT assets in a centralized ledger.    Ensure regular updates of equipment configurations and connections.    Identify critical components that require enhanced protection

Establish indicators to measure the effectiveness of the security program.       Define KPIs (Key Performance Indicators) to track compliance with cybersecurity policies.    Conduct regular audits to assess the performance of security measures.    Use dashboards to monitor trends and identify areas for improvement.

Establish policies and procedures for the management of personnel security, including responsibilities and processes for the selection, hiring, evaluation, training and separation of employees.       Write a personnel security policy specific to OT systems.   Train staff on the safety requirements of operations.   Periodically evaluate the effectiveness of procedures.

Identify critical positions and assign a level of risk based on their responsibilities and access to sensitive resources.    Use industry-specific regulations to define risk levels.   Perform a job analysis to determine safety requirements.   Regularly update risk designations based on evolving threats.

Conduct background checks on employees and contractors based on their level of access to OT systems.       Implement a pre-employment background check process.   Perform periodic checks for employees in sensitive positions.   Apply enhanced checks for system administrators and other critical roles.

Define a secure employee departure management process to minimize security risks related to unauthorized residual access.       Immediately revoke access to OT systems after the departure notification.   Ensure the return of all equipment and access badges.   Conduct post-departure follow-up to ensure that no security breaches have occurred.

Manage the internal transfer of employees to adapt their access privileges to their new responsibilities.       Update the access rights of transferred employees.   Inform new departments of security responsibilities.   Verify that the old extension does not retain any residual access

Ensure that any employee or contractor with access to OT systems understands and agrees to the security requirements and associated responsibilities.       Draft clear and detailed access agreements.   Require the signing of a confidentiality and security compliance agreement before any access.   Conduct periodic reminders of user obligations

Apply specific controls for external service providers, subcontractors and consultants with access to critical infrastructure.       Impose background checks on contractors.   Restrict their access to only the resources necessary for their missions.   Implement security training and awareness sessions.

Define a disciplinary framework for non-compliance with security policies.       Establish a clear disciplinary procedure.   Communicate to employees the consequences of violations of safety rules.   Implement a follow-up of violations and penalties applied.

Ensure that each job description includes security responsibilities and requirements for the protection of critical assets.       Add a safety section in all job descriptions.   Clarify cybersecurity and OT protection expectations for each role.   Train employees on their specific responsibilities for OT security.

Define a policy and procedures for assessing cybersecurity risks in an OT environment.   Develop a policy adapted to OT systems, taking into account the interdependencies with IT systems.   Ensure that the policy covers threat assessments specific to industrial environments.   Train OT and IT teams on how to apply risk assessment procedures.

Determine the level of impact of OT systems based on potential threats and operational requirements.   Use Process Hazard Analysis (PHA) and Functional Safety Assessments.   Classify OT assets according to their criticality to production and safe operations.   Adapt protective measures according to the level of risk assigned to OT systems

Identify and assess cybersecurity risks based on potential threats, vulnerabilities, and impacts.   Perform regular risk assessments by integrating scenarios specific to OT environments (e.g. SCADA compromise).   Combine cybersecurity and industrial engineering experts for in-depth threat analysis.   Assess the impact of threats on critical infrastructure and business continuity.

Implement mechanisms to monitor and detect vulnerabilities in OT systems.   Perform vulnerability scans with tools adapted to OT environments (e.g. passive rather than active analysis to avoid disruptions).   Maintain an inventory of OT assets and cross-reference it with recognized vulnerability databases (CISA, NIST, NVD).   Plan vulnerability assessments during periods of planned shutdown of industrial systems

Determine the critical components of an OT environment and their impact in the event of a failure or attack.   Define criticality criteria based on production and safety implications.   Assess the interdependencies between OT and IT components to identify points of vulnerability.   Implement specific mitigation measures for assets identified as critical.

Establish policies and procedures to ensure that the procurement of systems and services takes into account OT security.   Write a policy covering OT specificities and its interactions with non-OT systems.   Integrate cybersecurity requirements from the procurement phase of OT equipment.

Determine the financial, human and technical resources required to ensure the security of acquisitions.   Assess costs and needs to secure existing and future OT systems.   Ensure adequate funding for the upgrade of critical equipment.   Allocate teams dedicated to the management and security of new acquisitions

Ensure that cybersecurity is integrated into every phase of the OT systems lifecycle.   Define a lifecycle management process that takes into account the longevity of OT equipment.   Work with third-party integrators to mitigate security risks.   Plan for technology updates to limit the use of outdated systems

Manage acquisitions to include cybersecurity requirements by design of OT systems.   Include cybersecurity clauses in acquisition contracts.   Take into account the security specifications and protocols used (e.g. SCADA).   Verify that purchased OT products comply with applicable standards (NIST, IEC 62443)

Ensure complete documentation of acquired systems to ensure their secure management.   Require vendors to provide documentation detailing the architecture, protocols, and potential vulnerabilities of acquired systems.   Set up an internal repository of OT equipment and available updates.   Train OT teams on documentation and secure use of new systems

Define policies and procedures to ensure the protection of OT systems and communications.   Develop a policy that incorporates the specific requirements for OT systems.   Include guidance on the use of secure protocols and defence-in-depth mechanisms.   Provide training for OT staff on the implementation of protection procedures

Manage network disconnection based on risk and operational needs.   Define scenarios for secure disconnection in the event of an incident.   Automate the cutting of unauthorized connections through real-time monitoring systems.   Regularly test logout procedures to ensure they are effective.

Ensure effective management of cryptographic keys used to secure OT communications.   Establish a key management process that aligns with industry best practices.   Use secure hardware modules (HSMs) to store and protect keys.   Regularly audit key management mechanisms to identify potential vulnerabilities.

Manage the risks of using collaborative applications in an OT environment.   Restrict the use of collaborative tools that could compromise the security of OT systems.   Verify that the applications used comply with industrial cybersecurity standards.   Disable non-essential functions on devices connected to critical systems.

Control Name: Separation of System and User Functionality
Control Description: Ensure the separation of administrative and operational functions of OT systems to minimize the risk of intrusion.   Set up separate accounts for the administration and operation of systems.   Use separate systems for OT management and operations.   Implement enhanced logging measures to detect anomalous activity.

Ensure the protection of sensitive data stored in OT systems.   Use encryption of sensitive data stored on industrial systems.   Restrict physical and logical access to critical data storage servers.   Set up secure backups to prevent data loss.

Ensure the isolation of security functions to prevent them from being compromised by unauthorized users.   Implement secure architectures with strong access controls.   Deploy OT equipment with dedicated security modules (e.g. industrial firewalls).   Regularly check that security features cannot be disabled by a standard user

Prevent sensitive information from leaking when resources are shared between different processes.   Restrict access to critical information to only authorized users and processes.   Implement mechanisms for segmenting and isolating OT systems.   Conduct audits to identify risks related to shared resources

Ensure synchronization of OT system clocks to ensure consistency of events and audit logs.   Use reliable reference time sources (e.g., GPS, IEEE 1588).   Implement centralized synchronization mechanisms for all OT equipment.   Regularly check timestamps for consistency in system and network logs

Implement communication alternatives to ensure business continuity in the event of an incident.   Define backup communication paths to ensure the resiliency of OT networks.   Regularly test backup communication mechanisms.   Train staff on the use of alternative routes in the event of a breakdown or attack

Protect OT systems from DoS attacks that can disrupt critical operations.   Prioritize protection against DoS attacks based on OT risk analysis.   Use industrial firewalls and anomaly detection systems to block attacks in advance.   Implement incident response plans to quickly restore services in the event of an attack

Secure OT system boundaries to prevent unauthorized access.   Segment OT and IT networks with separate security zones.   Deploy secure gateways to filter exchanges between OT and IT.   Use secure protocols and VPNs for traffic between industrial sites.

Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of OT communications in transit.   Implement encryption protocols for sensitive communications.   Verify that transmission mechanisms do not generate critical latency for OT operations.   Regularly assess the security of communication channels

Establish specific policies and procedures to ensure the integrity of OT systems and information.   Develop policies that take into account the specificities of OT and their relationship with IT systems.   Define processes for managing incidents related to the integrity of industrial systems.   Train OT teams on data integrity best practices

Ensure that data entered into OT systems is valid and does not contain malicious content.   Verify input data on critical interfaces (e.g. SCADA, HMI).   Implement filtering and validation mechanisms for orders sent to industrial equipment.   Restrict the types of input accepted to limit the risk of injection attacks

Ensure error handling that does not disclose sensitive information on OT systems.   Define error handling mechanisms specific to OT environments.   Avoid overly detailed error messages that can help an attacker.   Ensure critical errors trigger appropriate alerts.

Ensure the retention of critical information for the continuity and security of OT operations.   Define retention and archiving policies adapted to industrial systems.   Ensure restricted access to critical data.   Automate the backup of essential information to prevent data loss

Identify and mitigate potential causes of outages in OT systems.   Implement mechanisms to monitor hardware and software failures.   Perform risk analyses on critical components.   Plan preventive interventions on aging equipment

Identify, remediate, and manage vulnerabilities in OT systems while minimizing the impact on availability.   Implement validation and testing processes before patching.   Employ compensatory measures (e.g., network segmentation, access throttling) when patches are not available.   Follow the cybersecurity recommendations of specialized organizations (e.g. CISA, ICS-CERT)

Deploy malware protections without impacting critical OT system operations.   Check that the protection mechanisms do not affect the performance of industrial equipment.   Restrict the use of removable media and other potential vectors of infection.   Perform security scans on software updates before they are installed.

Implement monitoring mechanisms to detect suspicious activity and threats in real-time.   Deploy monitoring solutions adapted to OT environments (e.g. IDS specific to industrial networks).   Set up alerts on unusual events without generating disruptions.   Regularly audit security logs and access to critical systems.

Ensure effective updating and dissemination of OT cybersecurity alerts and recommendations.   Use cybersecurity alerts published by specialized agencies (e.g. CISA, ICS-CERT).   Integrate an active monitoring process on vulnerabilities impacting industrial equipment.   Train teams on emerging threat management and appropriate responses

Validate the effectiveness of the security mechanisms put in place on OT systems.   Plan periodic security tests in accordance with operational constraints.   Verify that protection mechanisms do not impact the availability of critical systems.   Document detected deviations and improvement plans

Ensure that software and firmware used in OT systems have not been tampered with.   Use digital signatures and integrity validation mechanisms.   Verify that updates are applied securely.   Implement real-time monitoring solutions to detect unauthorized changes

Prevent the intrusion of spam and other forms of unwanted traffic into OT systems.   Disable non-essential features like email and web browsing on OT systems.   Restrict access to network services to only necessary equipment.   Verify the effectiveness of spam controls applied to connected networks.

Develop policies and procedures to manage risks related to the supply chain of OT components.   Integrate cybersecurity controls into vendor selection.   Define evaluation criteria for incoming and produced components.   Implement compensating controls for OT systems using outdated components

Implement a process for systematically inspecting components before they are integrated into OT systems.   Require compliance certifications for critical equipment.   Verify the provenance and authenticity of components prior to installation.   Use analysis tools to detect possible software or hardware alterations

Ensure that components used in OT systems are authentic and free of counterfeits.   Implement authenticity validation processes, including verification of serial numbers and digital signatures.   Require suppliers to provide guarantees on the authenticity and traceability of components.   Actively monitor alerts about counterfeit components in the marketplace.

Ensure secure disposal of obsolete or compromised OT components to prevent unauthorized reuse.   Define a procedure for the secure destruction of critical components.   Follow e-waste disposal regulations.   Ensure traceability of disposed components to avoid potential leaks.

Establish a structured supply chain risk management plan, incorporating the identification and mitigation of potential threats.   Identify critical assets dependent on the supply chain.   Establish a team dedicated to supplier risk management.   Ensure continuous monitoring of threats affecting key suppliers.

Implement secure processes to minimize risk from third-party suppliers and components.   Diversify suppliers to avoid failures common to a single source.   Assess suppliers' manufacturing and cybersecurity practices.   Verify the conformity of components before they are integrated into OT systems.

Develop robust acquisition strategies to ensure the availability of critical components of OT systems.   Maintain a stock of critical spare parts to avoid interruptions in the event of a shortage.   Establish trusted partnerships with certified suppliers.   Verify the reliability of suppliers by conducting regular audits.

Conduct periodic vendor assessments to ensure compliance with OT security requirements.   Assess vendor cybersecurity posture through compliance audits.   Require safety reports on critical components.   Set up a watch to identify potential vulnerabilities in suppliers.

Establish agreements with vendors to ensure transparency and timely communication in the event of vulnerabilities or security incidents.   Require vendors to provide prompt notification when vulnerabilities are discovered in their products.   Define SLAs (Service Level Agreements) to govern incident response and remediation times.   Proactively monitor cybersecurity alerts affecting OT components.

Implement measures to detect any physical or software tampering with OT components throughout their lifecycle.   Verify the integrity of the equipment received by implementing authenticity checks.   Deploy mechanisms to detect unauthorized changes to critical components.   Raise awareness among operators to identify signs of physical tampering on industrial equipment.

Administrative Safeguards: Defined in the Security Rule as the “administrative actions and policies, and procedures to manage the selection, development, implementation, and maintenance of security measures to protect electronic protected health information and to manage the conduct of the covered entity's workforce in relation to the protection of that information.”
Security Management Process: HIPAA Standard: Implement policies and procedures to prevent, detect, contain, and correct security violations.

Assigned Security Responsibility: HIPAA Standard: Identify the security official who is responsible for the development and implementation of the policies and procedures required by this subpart for the covered entity or business associate.

Workforce Security: HIPAA Standard: Implement policies and procedures to ensure that all members of its workforce have appropriate access to electronic protected health information, as provided under paragraph (a)(4) of this section, and to prevent those workforce members who do not have access under paragraph (a)(4) of this section from obtaining access to electronic protected health information.

Information Access Management: HIPAA Standard: Implement policies and procedures for authorizing access to electronic protected health information that are consistent with the applicable requirements of subpart E of this part.
Security Awareness and Training: HIPAA Standard: Implement a security awareness and training program for all members of its workforce (including management).
Security Incident Procedures: HIPAA Standard: Implement policies and procedures to address security incidents.

Contingency Plan: HIPAA Standard: Establish (and implement as needed) policies and procedures for responding to an emergency or other occurrence (for example, fire, vandalism, system failure, and natural disaster) that damages systems that contain electronic protected health information

Evaluation: HIPAA Standard: Perform a periodic technical and nontechnical evaluation, based initially upon the standards implemented under this rule and subsequently, in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information, that establishes the extent to which a covered entity’s or business associate’s security policies and procedures meet the requirements of this subpart.

Business Associate Contracts and Other Arrangements: HIPAA Standard: A covered entity may permit a business associate to create, receive, maintain, or transmit electronic protected health information on the covered entity’s behalf only if the covered entity obtains satisfactory assurances, in accordance with § 164.314(a), that the business associate will appropriately safeguard the information. A covered entity is not required to obtain such satisfactory assurances from a business associate that is a subcontractor.

Physical Safeguards: Defined as the “physical measures, policies, and procedures to protect a covered entity’s electronic information systems and related buildings and equipment, from natural and environmental hazards, and unauthorized intrusion.”

Facility Access Controls: HIPAA Standard: Implement policies and procedures to limit physical access to its electronic information systems and the facility or facilities in which they are housed, while ensuring that properly authorized access is allowed.

Workstation Use: HIPAA Standard: Implement policies and procedures that specify the proper functions to be performed, the manner in which those functions are to be performed, and the physical attributes of the surroundings of a specific workstation or class of workstation that can access electronic protected health information.
Workstation Security: HIPAA Standard: Implement physical safeguards for all workstations that access electronic protected health information, to restrict access to authorized users.

Device and Media Controls: HIPAA Standard: Implement policies and procedures that govern the receipt and removal of hardware and electronic media that contain electronic protected health information into and out of a facility, and the movement of these items within the facility.
Technical Safeguards: Defined as the “the technology and the policy and procedures for its use that protect electronic protected health information and control access to it.”

Access Control: HIPAA Standard: Implement technical policies and procedures for electronic information systems that maintain electronic protected health information to allow access only to those persons or software programs that have been granted access rights as specified in § 164.308(a)(4).

Audit Controls: HIPAA Standard: Implement hardware, software, and/or procedural mechanisms that record and examine activity in information systems that contain or use electronic protected health information.
Integrity: HIPAA Standard: Implement policies and procedures to protect electronic protected health information from improper alteration or destruction.
Person or Entity Authentication: HIPAA Standard: Implement procedures to verify that a person or entity seeking access to electronic protected health information is the one claimed.

Transmission Security: HIPAA Standard: Implement technical security measures to guard against unauthorized access to electronic protected health information that is being transmitted over an electronic communications network.

Organizational Requirements: Includes standards for business associate contracts and other arrangements between a covered entity and a business associate and between a business associate and a subcontractor, as well as requirements for group health plans.

Business Associate Contracts or Other Arrangements: HIPAA Standard: (i) The contract or other arrangement between the covered entity and its business associate required by § 164.308(b)(3) must meet the requirements of paragraph (a)(2)(i), (a)(2)(ii), or (a)(2)(iii) of this section, as applicable. (ii) A covered entity is in compliance with paragraph (a)(1) of this section if it has another arrangement in place that meets the requirements of § 164.504(e)(3). (iii) The requirements of paragraphs (a)(2)(i) and (a)(2)(ii) of this section apply to the contract or other arrangement between a business associate and a subcontractor required by § 164.308(b)(4) in the same manner as such requirements apply to contracts or other arrangements between a covered entity and business associate.
